text:
David Pastrnak has 24 points in 18 games, but the shape of them has changed: 16 assists and 8 goals, with his shooting at 12.5%, right around his normal range. He's become the setup half of what Daily Faceoff calls one of the league's elite duos, with Pavel Zacha finishing more of the plays.

Here's the caution. Boston has scored 8.5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that's padding the point total. The Bruins' five-on-five share with him, 53% of expected goals, is good rather than dominant.

The talent isn't in doubt. Evolving-Hockey had him 26th among 401 forwards last season while playing against the other team's best and with weaker teammates, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him getting to the home-plate area more than most. He's still a 100-point player by last season's line. Watch the assists: when teammates' shooting cools, his point pace will tell you how much of this was him.
headline: Pastrnak is setting the table, with help
